experiment: Track 3 Clean Re-run with N_STEPS Fix
n_steps_fix: N_STEPS changed from 200 to 999999 (coordinator controls via MSG_END). Previous matches had workers exiting at step 200 while coordinator ran 1242+ steps, producing stale data for 84% of match.

rl_policy.name: chase_v8_policy.onnx + t1_walk.pt
rl_policy.rl_components: locomotion (t1_walk.pt, frozen PPO) + chase direction (chase_v8 ONNX, 19→3 MLP)
rl_policy.rule_components: role assignment, kick dash, goalkeeper, defender positioning

E_clean_60s.note: 1 goal scored by rule team (own-goal scenario: ball reached x=-8.0, left goal)

same_architecture_recovery_comparison.note: RL team recovery is comparable to rule team in same architecture. Both use t1_walk.pt.

summary.goal_scoring: 0 RL goals in 18 clean matches. 1 rule goal (ball entered left goal at x=-8.0). Ball max X for RL team: 5.9m (goal at 7.0m). 25s matches too short for ball to reach goal.

honest_assessment: The clean re-run confirms: (1) Platform stability: 0 abnormal exits in 18 matches. (2) Recovery: 83-93% rate with t1_walk.pt. (3) No RL scoring advantage: 0 goals in 18 matches. (4) Ball progression: RL+kick pushes ball forward (max 5.9m) but not enough to score in 25s. (5) The project is a failure recovery and OOD evaluation platform, not a competitive soccer policy.
